key_insight: ZeoBench introduces a benchmark for studying self-supervised learning on 3D zeolite representations. Its central motivation is to learn from abundant structures when expensive property labels are scarce.
problem_solved: Finding zeolites suited to gas storage, separations, or catalysis is difficult because property measurements are costly and available for only a limited set of structure–molecule pairs.
method: Focus on 3D representations of porous crystalline zeolite structures.
Benchmark self-supervised learning as a way to exploit structural data without requiring property labels for every example.
Specific architectures, training objectives, evaluation tasks, and results are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ZeoBench offers a benchmark focused on representation learning for label-scarce materials discovery. It could help assess whether structural pretraining improves downstream property prediction, though the supplied excerpt does not establish performance gains.

Data imbalance graphic: many known structures versus few labeled structure–molecule pairs.
Conceptual pipeline: unlabeled 3D structures → self-supervised representations → property prediction.
Application icons for gas storage, molecular separation, and catalysis.
paper_title: ZeoBench: A Benchmark for Self-Supervised Learning on 3D Zeolite Representations
paper_authors: Aaron Sun, Yachan Liu, Ping Yang, Peng Bai, Subhransu Maji
